candidates: Do not wrap static, never-changing data in `ref()` or `reactive()` in Vue components. Use a plain `const` for data that is set once and never mutated; reserve `ref`/`reactive` for values that actually change over the component's lifetime.

Avoid identifying clickable elements inside global DOM event listeners by matching `target.textContent`. This coupling breaks silently whenever the displayed text changes. Instead, use `data-*` attributes, a dedicated CSS class, or component-level `@click` handlers to mark and detect the intended target.

When a global `click` (or `mousedown`) event listener intercepts an anchor-tag click in order to show a UI overlay instead of navigating, always call `e.preventDefault()` — and `e.stopPropagation()` where appropriate — to prevent the browser from following the link.

Be explicit about whether `v-if` or `v-show` is the right directive for toggling UI element visibility. Use `v-if` when the element truly should not exist in the DOM while hidden; use `v-show` for elements that are toggled frequently (e.g., modals) to avoid repeated mount/unmount cost. Add a comment when the choice is non-obvious.

Keep all component data, configuration objects, and hardcoded display strings inside `<script setup>` rather than scattered as inline literals in the `<template>` block. The template should reference named variables; it should not be the authoritative source of data.

In this project's Vue SFC components, use Tailwind utility classes exclusively for styling. Do not mix Tailwind classes with inline `style=""` attributes or `<style>` scoped blocks on the same elements; resolve conflicts by finding the correct Tailwind utility rather than falling back to raw CSS.

Static assets (SVG icons, images) referenced in Vue components must be checked into the repository — place them under `docs/public/icons/` and `packages/mermaid/src/docs/public/icons/` so both the docs site and the source tree are in sync. Never reference icons or images via external third-party URLs.

Do not append UTM or other tracking query parameters to `mermaid.live/edit` URLs. The live editor stores the diagram state in the URL's hash/query string, so tracking parameters corrupt any diagram link shared by users. Use clean URLs (e.g., `https://mermaid.live/edit`) for the live editor.

In Tailwind-styled Vue components, prefer `flex` with `gap-*` utilities to create spacing between sibling elements rather than applying individual `mr-*`, `ml-*`, `mt-*`, or `mb-*` margin utilities on each child. Flex-gap is easier to read, avoids bleeding margins, and keeps spacing logic in one place.

Do not use a `v-for` array index to derive semantic meaning (e.g., `index === 1` to decide which card is highlighted). Add an explicit boolean or descriptive property directly to the data model (e.g., `highlighted: true`) and reference that property in the template. Remove all index-based conditional logic from templates.
